explanation: Roasting zinc sulphide ore strongly in excess air converts it to zinc oxide, releasing sulphur dioxide gas — the step that must happen before zinc oxide can be reduced to metallic zinc with carbon.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Zinc sulphide ore (colour varies considerably with impurities — shown here as a generic brownish-grey).
beaker_view.observation: Roasted strongly in air, the ore gives off sulphur dioxide fumes and turns into white zinc oxide.
